newsitem.title: UK: Vickers profits rise, but company cautious.
newsitem.headline: Vickers profits rise, but company cautious.

text.p: Vickers Plc Wednesday announced an 11 percent rise in annual profits but the maker of Rolls-Royce cars and Challenger tanks cautioned that the pound sterling's recent strength clouded the outlook for its export-driven business in 1997.
Pretax profits in 1996 increased to 83.3 million pounds ($132.4 million) on sales up 4.7 percent at 1.97 billion pounds ($3.14 billion).

"1996 represented a competent performance for the Vickers Group as a whole," chairman Sir Richard Lloyd said in a statement accompanying the results. "These results were achieved in the context of a demanding investment programme, which saw further substantial expenditure during 1996."

But he added: "Because of the effects on export orders and earnings of the rise in the trade-weighted value of sterling against other currencies which began last autumn, it is unusually difficult to foresee the trends of sales and profits in 1997."
However, Lloyd added, over the next two years the strategies for each business were now "thoroughly founded," and so "another better performance should be achieved."
